newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Peso next target of speculators after baht - SocGen.
newsitem.headline: Peso next target of speculators after baht - SocGen.

text.p: The Philippines peso is likely to be the next target of speculative selling pressure now that the baht has effectively been devalued, the head of research at SocGen-Crosby Securities said on Thursday.
Manu Bhaskaran told a briefing in Singapore the peso was overvalued and likely to slip five to six percent over the next six months from its current position around 26.4 to the dollar.
He said speculative pressures would build up on the currency following the shock announcement on Wednesday that the Thai currency would be subject to a "managed float" on foreign exchange markets.

"Clearly the peso will be the main target now," Bhaskaran said. "It is the one (other) currency in Southeast Asia which we would see as overvalued. The natural pressures could see some correction...perhaps five or six percent over six months."
By the end of 1997, he expected the peso to be around 28.50.

Bhaskaran said the Philippines peso was vulnerable because the country's foreign exchange reserves were not as strong as some of its neighbours and its balance of payments had weakened in recent months:
"We think the peso will have to come down at some time."

He said the baht -- which was trading around 28.50 to the U.S. dollar in offshore markets by 0700 GMT on Thursday, from 25.85 just before the government's announcement -- was likely to slip to around 30 to the dollar by the end of the year.
The baht crisis would also squeeze interest rates around the region, he said.
"It pre-disposes interest rates to be higher -- with the exception of in Singapore," he said.
The Singapore dollar would probably gain from its status as a safe home in turbulent times, he said.
